label: France — Côte d'Azur
summary: The Côte d'Azur is now modeled as a cluster of distinct premium nodes — Nice (the air gateway), Monaco, Antibes (Europe's largest yacht harbour), Cannes (Film + Yachting Festival) and St-Tropez — packed into a short, ultra-affluent coastal strip where the corniche roads jam constantly and a yacht-conditioned clientele already values water transfer. Anchor on the Cannes/Antibes yacht hubs, scale through the Nice gateway and Monaco with the Nice Airport–Monaco corporate run, and reach St-Tropez and the cross-border Sanremo/Portofino legs. Bolt's French presence is the front door.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Côte d'Azur
hero.subtitle: Foil the Riviera from Cannes to Monaco at speed, booked in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling tier across the Côte d'Azur cluster — Cannes, Antibes, Nice, Monaco, St-Tropez and Menton — anchored on the Cannes/Antibes yacht hubs, with the Nice Airport–Monaco corporate run and cross-border Sanremo/Portofino reach.

why_now: The Riviera is one of the densest concentrations of wealth and yachting on earth; the corniche roads are chronically congested and the Nice Airport–Monaco helicopter/road transfer is a premium pain point. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears every Riviera leg.
multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app: a Bolt car to the jetty, a foiling hop to Monaco or down the coast, seamless return — the premium chain on the corridors where the corniche is slowest and the clientele richest.
partner_context: Bolt operates in France and is expanding premium ambitions. The Côte d'Azur offers the highest willingness-to-pay coastal market in Europe, an ideal place for a co-branded marine tier.
why_navier_now: Every Riviera leg (Menton–Monaco 4nm, Antibes–Cannes 6nm, Nice Airport–Monaco 6.7nm, Monaco–Sanremo 13nm) is inside Pioneer II range — the whole network runs on the commercial-now hull.
differentiation: Against the corniche road and the airport helicopter: comparable or better cost, faster jetty-to-jetty, with zero local emissions. Against the yacht tender: an on-demand, in-app shared premium tier.

proof_points.claim: The Côte d'Azur is Europe's densest wealth-and-yachting coast.
proof_points.evidence: Cannes, Antibes, Nice and Monaco concentrate extreme willingness-to-pay along a short strip.

proof_points.claim: The Riviera legs are short by water.
Nice Airport–Monaco is a premium transfer pain point.
proof_points.evidence: Today served by helicopter and a congested road; a 6.7nm water leg is a direct substitute.
Monaco–Sanremo is a ~13nm Pioneer-range cross-border leg.

objections.concern: The clientele already has yachts and helicopters.
objections.response: Exactly the point: an on-demand, in-app foiling tier is faster than the road and cheaper and greener than the helicopter, capturing the transfers between owning a yacht and queuing on the corniche.

objections.concern: Monaco has strict marine access rules.
objections.response: We operate within licensed berths and Monaco's access framework; low-wake all-electric foiling aligns with its environmental positioning.

objections.concern: The market is seasonal around events.
objections.response: Demand peaks around the Grand Prix, the film festival and summer, but year-round corporate Nice Airport–Monaco transfers provide a steady base.

the_ask: Co-brand a Côte d'Azur water tier with Bolt — a 2-boat Pioneer II anchor across the Cannes/Antibes yacht hubs, scaling through the Nice gateway and Monaco with the Nice Airport–Monaco corporate run, then reaching St-Tropez and the cross-border Sanremo/Portofino legs.
close: The Riviera is the world's richest congested coast — a Bolt-branded foiling tier beats both the corniche and the helicopter on the corridors that matter most.
end_state: A Cannes/Antibes-to-St-Tropez Riviera network anchored on the yacht hubs and the Nice gateway, with the Nice Airport–Monaco corporate run and cross-border Sanremo/Portofino legs, all booked in the Bolt app.

phases.label: Phase 1 — Prove (Cannes + Antibes yacht-hub anchor, Pioneer II)
phases.vessel: N30 Pioneer II (8 pax, commercial now)
phases.narrative: Launch the Cannes anchor and the adjacent Antibes superyacht hub on Pioneer II — the captive Lérins island shuttle and the Antibes↔Cannes hop between Europe's two densest yacht harbours.
phases.rationale: Dense, ultra-high-value, short coastal water with a congested-corniche incumbent.

phases.label: Phase 2 — Scale the Pioneer II network (Nice gateway + Monaco, N30 + N35 Shuttle)
phases.vessel: N30 Pioneer II + N35 Shuttle (12–15 pax, 2027) on dense legs
phases.narrative: Bring in the Nice gateway and Monaco: add the marquee Nice Airport↔Monaco corporate run, the Nice↔Monaco and Nice↔Cannes coastal links, the Menton/Villefranche↔Monaco hops and the cross-border Monaco↔Sanremo leg, with N35 on the densest corridors.
phases.rationale: Captures the marquee Monaco corridor and the airport corporate transfer.

phases.label: Phase 3 — Regional reach (Quanta-LR, 75–150nm) + St-Tropez + mature in-app capture
phases.vessel: N35-led mix; Quanta-LR on 75–150nm regional legs
phases.narrative: Open the Gulf of St-Tropez (Cannes↔St-Tropez ~30nm, Nice↔St-Tropez ~45nm — beating the notorious summer road) and the cross-border Quanta-LR legs (Monaco↔Sanremo, Monaco↔Portofino), and mature in-app capture across the corridor.
phases.rationale: Pioneer-range cross-border reach plus default-operator monetization.
